successors.name: Hittite Empire
successors.text: Qatna sacked by Suppiluliuma I after the palace was burned in 1340 BC; the Hittite shape of -1300 is the first to reach the Orontes

ledger.x: c. 2000 BC: the Amorite kingdom of Qatna is established. 'In the Middle Bronze, the Kingdom of Qatna was established around 2000 BC'; the site was first occupied in the Late Chalcolithic IV (3300-3000 BC). A round number, not a founding act.
16th century BC: Qatna becomes a Mitannian vassal.

c. 1446 BC (bridged): Mitanni's hold ends as Egypt's begins. The page has no end for the Mitannian vassalage; Thutmose III 'reached Qatna during his eighth Asiatic campaign, c. 1446 BC' and 'established vassalage ties', and the Thutmose III page puts the Euphrates crossing in his regnal year 33 and makes no mention of…

c. 1446 BC: Thutmose III makes Qatna an Egyptian vassal. 'Thutmose III reached Qatna during his eighth Asiatic campaign, c. 1446 BC, and established vassalage ties'; Amenhotep II later 'fought troops from Qatna near the city' in his seventh regnal year (undated). Akizzi still wrote to Akhenaten c. 1334 BC.

c. 1337 BC (bridged): Qatna falls to Hatti while its king Akizzi pleads with Egypt (letter EA 55, 'before the death of Akhenaten, to whom the letter was addressed, in c. 1334 BC'); the sack falls between the palace's destruction in 1340 BC and the letter.

c. 1337 BC: Suppiluliuma I sacks Qatna. 'The final sack of Qatna occurred after the royal palace was destroyed in 1340 BC', attributed to Suppiluliuma I who came with Aziru of Amurru. The Suppiluliuma I page lists Qatna among the kingdoms he conquered across the Euphrates, with no year; his reign is 'c. 1350-1322 BC'.

c. 1337 BC: the kingdom of Qatna ends. The tell is then 'uninhabited for about three centuries', reoccupied in the late 10th century BC and destroyed by the Assyrians in 720 BC (Aramean phase, not drawn).

wars.name: Yamhad's invasion of Qatna
wars.outcome: 'In the late 17th century BC, Yamhad invaded and defeated Qatna during the reign of Yarim-Lim III'; the Yamhad page has Qatna 'remained independent, then made peace with Yamhad under Yarim-Lim III'.

wars.name: Thutmose III's eighth campaign
wars.outcome: Egypt 'established vassalage ties' with Qatna; no territory changes owners.

wars.name: Tushratta's attack on Qatna
wars.outcome: 'The Mitannian king Tushratta retaliated by invading Qatna, and burning the royal palace; an event dated to around 1340 BC.'

wars.name: Suppiluliuma I's Syrian war: the sack of Qatna
wars.outcome: Qatna plundered by Suppiluliuma I (with Aziru of Amurru) after 1340 BC and before Akizzi's letter of c.

certainty.note: No boundary is described; the Orontes valley, Qadesh and Palmyra are named only as places.
